### Workload: q13 only (customer LEFT JOIN orders with NOT LIKE '%a%b%' filter, count per key, then count per count)
Current best (after E0004): about 458-476ms hot (1.551x). Operator CPU: orders TABLE_SCAN with LIKE 2.37s; PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY 0.46s; HASH_JOIN (perfect, RIGHT) 0.22s; decompress_bigint projection above the join 0.17s; outer HASH_GROUP_BY 0.07s. Fully parallel (CPU/8 is about wall).
Baseline was about 784ms.

### Scan cost breakdown (round 5 microbenchmarks, scan operator CPU at 8 threads on orders)
- o_custkey+o_orderkey only: 0.41s
- + o_comment decode (length>45 filter): 1.92s, so decode is about 1.5s, about 100ns/string, far above FSST decoder speed.
- NOT contains: 2.23-2.44s; q13 NOT LIKE: 2.36s. So the matcher costs about 0.3-0.5s.
- threads=1: 2.09s, so the cost is per-row compute, not bandwidth.
- SET enable_fsst_vectors=true is slower (2.93s). The default is off, so the scan decodes eagerly via StringScanPartial<false>.
- `length(o_comment) > 3` is pruned by stats, so use a selective threshold for tests.

### Round 6 hypothesis for the decode overhead (dispatched)
- FSSTPrimitives::DecompressValue (common/fsst.hpp:36) does arena AllocateShrinkableBuffer(len*8) for each string on the result vector's VectorStringBuffer.
- The vector auxiliary is fresh every chunk (StringVector::GetStringBuffer, vector.cpp:2218). Its ArenaAllocator starts at 2KB and doubles (arena_allocator.cpp:63), so about 7 mallocs of up to 256KB per vector, with cold or mmapped pages. No jemalloc is loaded (glibc malloc).
- ArenaAllocator::Reset keeps the head block, so reuse gives zero mallocs after warm-up.
- The fix caches a VectorStringBuffer in FSSTScanState and reuses it when use_count()==1.
- If it fails with no gain, the allocation theory is wrong and the overhead is elsewhere (bitunpack or delta decode per call? FetchStringPointer?).

### Facts learned
- CanUsePerfectHashAggregate: plan_aggregate.cpp:127. perfect_ht_threshold defaults to 12; settings defaults are off limits.
- PerfectAggregateHashTable allocates outside the buffer manager, so it needs a memory guard.
- Perfect hash join: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp CanDoPerfectHashJoin now handles INNER+RIGHT, up to 2^22 dense.
- Filter scan path: RowGroup::Scan -> StandardColumnData::Filter. FSST has no compression->filter, so the path is Scan + ToUnifiedFormat + ColumnSegment::FilterSelection (EXPRESSION_FILTER at column_segment.cpp:563).
- FSST scan: FSSTStorage::StringScanPartial (fsst.cpp:645), FSSTScanState::DecompressString (fsst.cpp:556), all_values_inlined fast path when max len <= 12.
- LikeMatcher::Match (like.cpp:231) -> FindStrInStr (contains.cpp:76).
- dbe-tool sql accepts "SET ...; EXPLAIN ANALYZE ...". One dbe-tool call per Bash call.
- Wall noise on q13 is ±15%; acceptance needs at least -5%.

### Experiments
- E0001 dense-range PHA: RETIRED -3.6% (it needed a parallel combine/source).
- E0002 conditional found-match store: no gain. Don't retry.
- E0003 parallel combine + source for large PHA: ACCEPTED -20.1%.
- E0004 perfect HJ for RIGHT joins: ACCEPTED -19.3%.
- E0005 SWAR/SSE2 first+last-byte strstr: RETIRED at -4.8% official, although the implementer's bench said -11.8%. It is a good idea that missed narrowly. Worth re-landing combined with an AVX2 path or another scan win.
- Round 6 dispatched: FSST string heap reuse (see above).

### Directions
- Scan decode (about 1.5s) is the biggest item; see the round 6 hypothesis.
- Re-land E0005 (maybe plus AVX2) once the decode overhead is cut; the matcher's share then grows.
- Backlog: remove the cancelling compress/decompress projection pair (0.17s, -3 to -5%, near noise).
- PHA: per-thread init of 2M slots plus a scan of every slot (0.46s); lazy local tables or an occupancy bitmap could help a little.

issues.title: Reuse a per-scan-state string heap for FSST decoded strings
issues.hypothesis: In q13 the orders TABLE_SCAN costs 2.37s of the roughly 3.3s operator CPU. Round 5 microbenchmarks put o_comment decode at about 1.5s, about 100ns per string, which is far above the FSST decoder's speed of about 1 cycle per byte, and the overhead was never explained. In FSSTStorage::StringScanPartial<false> (src/storage/compression/fsst.cpp:696-701), every non-inlined string goes through FSSTPrimitives::DecompressValue (src/include/duckdb/common/fsst.hpp:36). That calls VectorStringBuffer::AllocateShrinkableBuffer(len*8) on the result vector's string heap. The scan vector's auxiliary is dropped on every chunk reset, so StringVector::GetStringBuffer (vector.cpp:2218) makes a fresh VectorStringBuffer whose ArenaAllocator starts at 2KB. ArenaAllocator::AllocateNewBlock (arena_allocator.cpp:63) doubles the block size, so each 2048-row vector of ~50-byte strings (about 100KB, plus len*8 headroom) does about 7 mallocs of 4KB to 256KB. It also wastes the leftover space of every old block. The larger blocks come from glibc malloc (no jemalloc is loaded), which serves them as fresh, often mmapped pages, so the scan page-faults and touches cold memory on every vector. Keeping one heap per scan state and reusing it when nobody else holds a reference fixes this: after warm-up, ArenaAllocator::Reset (arena_allocator.cpp:136) keeps the largest head block, so later vectors do zero mallocs into hot, already-mapped memory.
issues.plan:
In src/storage/compression/fsst.cpp:
1) Add `buffer_ptr<VectorStringBuffer> cached_string_buffer;` to FSSTScanState.
2) In StringScanPartial, in the non-FSST-vector branch (line 696), before calling StringVector::GetStringBuffer, check three conditions: result_offset == 0, result has no auxiliary yet, and the vector type is FLAT. If they all hold:
   - If cached_string_buffer exists and cached_string_buffer.use_count() == 1, meaning no downstream vector or chunk still references it, reset its heap. Add a small `void Reset()` to StringHeap that calls allocator.Reset(), and expose it on VectorStringBuffer.
   - Otherwise create a new one, with make_buffer<VectorStringBuffer>() or with the result buffer's allocator, the same way GetStringBuffer does.
   - Then set result's auxiliary to cached_string_buffer. Use the existing setter if there is one (grep for SetAuxiliary in vector.hpp); otherwise use StringVector::AddBuffer semantics, or assign `result.auxiliary` through a friend or accessor.
   - Then proceed as before.
   Do not touch the case where result_offset > 0 (a scan continuing in the same vector across segments): keep the existing buffer there.
3) Optionally, reserve once per call to avoid the doubling chain on first use: sum the compressed lengths for this call, multiply by 8, and pre-grow the arena with a single Allocate and ShrinkHead, so there is one block per vector instead of seven.
Correctness: use_count()==1 guarantees nothing else holds the strings. Operators that keep strings (hash tables, sorts, Vector::Reference copies) either hold a reference to the auxiliary, which raises use_count so we don't reuse, or copy the strings into their own heaps. Check that DataChunk/Vector Reference and Slice share the auxiliary buffer_ptr rather than copying raw pointers. If any path copies string_t without the auxiliary, the reuse is unsafe there; check this with grep on `auxiliary` in vector.cpp.
Validate with:
- the q13 bench
- SELECT of the full o_comment column with ORDER BY/LIMIT, and string_agg over a group by
- a hash join with string payload, which must keep its strings after the scan advances
- CREATE TABLE AS SELECT of the column, compared by hash against the original
Compare all of these with checksums such as sum(hash(o_comment)) under the old and new builds.
issues.expected_gain: q13: if the allocation and page-fault overhead is a large part of the 1.5s decode, about -10 to -20% wall (scan is about 70% of CPU). At minimum it saves the 7 mallocs per vector, so likely at least -5%.
issues.generality: Every scan of an FSST-compressed VARCHAR column with non-inlined strings, which covers most string columns in persistent DuckDB databases: comments, names, addresses. It helps filters, projections and string aggregations. Nothing should get slower: when the buffer is still referenced downstream, it falls back to a fresh buffer exactly as today. The only cost is one cached heap per scan state, at most about 16MB if one vector held huge strings.
issues.risk: Medium. The main risk is a use-after-free if some downstream path keeps string_t pointers without holding the vector's auxiliary buffer_ptr. The use_count check covers every holder that keeps a reference. Hidden-query correctness checks will catch the rest. Memory held per scan thread is bounded by the largest vector's decoded size.

## Memory (planner notes)

### Workload: q13 only (customer LEFT JOIN orders with NOT LIKE '%a%b%' filter, count per key, then count per count)
Current best (after E0004): about 458-476ms hot (1.551x). Operator CPU: orders TABLE_SCAN with LIKE 2.37s; PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY 0.46s; HASH_JOIN (perfect, RIGHT) 0.22s; decompress_bigint projection above the join 0.17s; outer HASH_GROUP_BY 0.07s. Fully parallel (CPU/8 is about wall).
Baseline was about 784ms.

- o_custkey+o_orderkey only: 0.41s
- + o_comment decode (length>45 filter): 1.92s, so decode is about 1.5s, about 100ns/string, far above FSST decoder speed.
- NOT contains: 2.23-2.44s; q13 NOT LIKE: 2.36s. So the matcher costs about 0.3-0.5s.
- threads=1: 2.09s, so the cost is per-row compute, not bandwidth.
- SET enable_fsst_vectors=true is slower (2.93s). The default is off, so the scan decodes eagerly via StringScanPartial<false>.
- `length(o_comment) > 3` is pruned by stats, so use a selective threshold for tests.

### Round 6 hypothesis for the decode overhead (dispatched)
- FSSTPrimitives::DecompressValue (common/fsst.hpp:36) does arena AllocateShrinkableBuffer(len*8) for each string on the result vector's VectorStringBuffer.
- The vector auxiliary is fresh every chunk (StringVector::GetStringBuffer, vector.cpp:2218). Its ArenaAllocator starts at 2KB and doubles (arena_allocator.cpp:63), so about 7 mallocs of up to 256KB per vector, with cold or mmapped pages. No jemalloc is loaded (glibc malloc).
- ArenaAllocator::Reset keeps the head block, so reuse gives zero mallocs after warm-up.
- The fix caches a VectorStringBuffer in FSSTScanState and reuses it when use_count()==1.
- If it fails with no gain, the allocation theory is wrong and the overhead is elsewhere (bitunpack or delta decode per call? FetchStringPointer?).

### Facts learned
- CanUsePerfectHashAggregate: plan_aggregate.cpp:127. perfect_ht_threshold defaults to 12; settings defaults are off limits.
- PerfectAggregateHashTable allocates outside the buffer manager, so it needs a memory guard.
- Perfect hash join: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp CanDoPerfectHashJoin now handles INNER+RIGHT, up to 2^22 dense.
- Filter scan path: RowGroup::Scan -> StandardColumnData::Filter. FSST has no compression->filter, so the path is Scan + ToUnifiedFormat + ColumnSegment::FilterSelection (EXPRESSION_FILTER at column_segment.cpp:563).
- FSST scan: FSSTStorage::StringScanPartial (fsst.cpp:645), FSSTScanState::DecompressString (fsst.cpp:556), all_values_inlined fast path when max len <= 12.
- LikeMatcher::Match (like.cpp:231) -> FindStrInStr (contains.cpp:76).
- dbe-tool sql accepts "SET ...; EXPLAIN ANALYZE ...". One dbe-tool call per Bash call.
- Wall noise on q13 is ±15%; acceptance needs at least -5%.

### Experiments
- E0001 dense-range PHA: RETIRED -3.6% (it needed a parallel combine/source).
- E0002 conditional found-match store: no gain. Don't retry.
- E0003 parallel combine + source for large PHA: ACCEPTED -20.1%.
- E0004 perfect HJ for RIGHT joins: ACCEPTED -19.3%.
- E0005 SWAR/SSE2 first+last-byte strstr: RETIRED at -4.8% official, although the implementer's bench said -11.8%. It is a good idea that missed narrowly. Worth re-landing combined with an AVX2 path or another scan win.
- Round 6 dispatched: FSST string heap reuse (see above).

### Directions
- Scan decode (about 1.5s) is the biggest item; see the round 6 hypothesis.
- Re-land E0005 (maybe plus AVX2) once the decode overhead is cut; the matcher's share then grows.
- Backlog: remove the cancelling compress/decompress projection pair (0.17s, -3 to -5%, near noise).
- PHA: per-thread init of 2M slots plus a scan of every slot (0.46s); lazy local tables or an occupancy bitmap could help a little.
